question.worked_solution:
First, we write $2\,\frac{2}{3}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{2}{3}=\frac{(2\times 3)+2}{3}=\frac{8}{3}
$$

We also write $10\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
10\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{(10\times 2)+1}{2}=\frac{21}{2}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3}\times \frac{21}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3}\times \frac{21}{2} & =\frac{8}{2}\times \frac{21}{3} \\  & =4\times 7 \\  & =28\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
2\,\frac{2}{3}\times 10\,\frac{1}{2}=28.
$$
